content.user_title: Improve QA Coverage With Test Automation
content.value_statement: Teams often miss coverage gaps and repeat manual QA planning work. This skill provides testing guidance, scaffold scripts, and coverage reporting patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides QA strategy, test automation planning, and best-practice review for web application projects.
Provides three Python helper scripts for test suite generation, coverage analysis, and E2E test scaffolding workflows.
Validates a target path before producing a simple status report for the requested QA task.
Can print JSON report output to the terminal or write it to a caller-selected output file.
Documents common local development, analysis, Docker, and Kubernetes commands used around QA workflows.
limitations: The helper scripts are scaffolds and do not implement deep test generation or coverage parsing.
The output file option does not prevent overwriting an existing path.
Reference documents contain generic placeholder patterns instead of framework-specific recipes.
The skill does not install dependencies or run test suites unless the user chooses those commands.

use_cases.title: Build a Test Strategy
use_cases.description: Create a structured QA plan that maps risks, test types, and quality gates for a new feature or release.

use_cases.title: Review Coverage Gaps
use_cases.description: Inspect an application area and produce a prioritized list of missing unit, integration, and E2E tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Quality Checks
use_cases.description: Turn manual validation needs into repeatable checks that fit local development and CI workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic QA Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use senior-qa to create a QA plan for [feature]. Include key risks, manual checks, and the first automated tests to add.

prompt_templates.title: Find Missing Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing project area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use senior-qa to review [project path or module]. Identify likely coverage gaps across unit, integration, and E2E testing.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Automation Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use senior-qa to design a test automation roadmap for [application]. Prioritize workflows, test layers, tooling, and CI checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use senior-qa to assess release readiness for [release scope]. Report blocking risks, recommended tests, quality metrics, and follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Review a React checkout flow before launch.
output: High-risk paths include payment errors, form validation, authentication state, and retry behavior.
Recommended tests include unit checks for validators, integration checks for cart totals, and E2E checks for successful and failed payment flows.
Release should wait until negative payment cases and abandoned checkout recovery are covered.

output_examples.input: Create a QA plan for a Next.js dashboard migration.
output: Start with route rendering, data loading, permission boundaries, and responsive layout checks.
Add automated coverage for dashboard filters, empty states, API failures, and navigation persistence.
Track readiness with pass rate, known defects, uncovered critical paths, and regression test completion.

output_examples.input: Assess whether Node.js API changes are ready for release.
output: Focus on contract changes, authorization checks, error responses, and backward compatibility.
Add integration tests for changed endpoints and E2E tests for user workflows that depend on them.
Block release if auth regressions, data loss paths, or undocumented breaking changes remain.

best_practices: Start with user risk and business impact before selecting test types.
Keep automated tests close to the workflow they protect and run them in CI.
Review coverage metrics with defect history, flaky tests, and release risk.
anti_patterns: Do not treat coverage percentage as proof that critical workflows are protected.
Do not add E2E tests for every small condition when unit or integration tests are clearer.
Do not run setup, deployment, or file-writing commands without checking the target project first.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests automatically?
faq.answer: It provides planning guidance and scaffold scripts. The included scripts are basic report tools, not full test generators.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It is most useful for React, Next.js, Node.js, and similar web application projects.

faq.question: Can it analyze real coverage reports?
faq.answer: The current scripts do not parse coverage files deeply. They can produce simple status output for a target path.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Will it run commands without approval?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents command examples, but execution should remain under user control.

faq.question: What should I review before using the scripts?
faq.answer: Check the target path, output path, dependency commands, and any project-specific test requirements.
